page: Microsoft Azure M64ms is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the MS server family. It is powered by a dedicated Intel Xeon 8280L processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The instance features 64 virtual CPUs mapped to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 1792.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a 2097 GB volume, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core CPU performance, measured via stress-ng and Geekbench, falls into the bottom 10% tier. However, multi-core CPU performance and Passmark CPU scores scale to average levels. Memory performance is a key highlight, with uncached large-block read bandwidth reaching a strong 196.25 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25% tier. Other memory operations, such as cached small-block reads and large-block writes, perform at average levels.

Given its massive memory capacity and average multi-core processing capabilities, the M64ms is designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads. It is highly suitable for large-scale relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and enterprise resource planning applications. The qualitative cost profile reflects a high-density resource allocation where the premium is placed on memory capacity rather than raw single-threaded CPU speed.
